entries.reconstructed_theorem: Let E be any complete real inner product space, with its compatible norm and additive group structure; no finite-dimensional hypothesis is imposed. Let f:E→ℝ and α,β,h∈ℝ be arbitrary. Assume (1) f is continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E; (2) for every x,y∈E and every t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y)−(α/2)t(1−t)‖y−x‖²; (3) α≥0; (4) β≥0; (5) h≥0; (6) βh≤1; and (7) for every x,y∈E, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖², where ∇f(x) is the Riesz vector representing the derivative of f at x. All these hypotheses hold globally and for the same fixed f,α,β,h. Define T(x)=x−h∇f(x), and q=Real.sqrt(1−αh), the nonnegative real square root with value zero on negative inputs. Then, for every x,y∈E, ‖T(y)−T(x)‖≤q‖y−x‖. Thus the declaration gives a uniform global one-step Lipschitz bound for the gradient update, with stated factor q depending only on α and h; β appears in the assumed upper quadratic model and step-size constraint. There are no other constants, restrictions on the two points, or dependence on dimension.
entries.notes: This statement asserts a one-step distance estimate, not the existence of a minimizer or fixed point, and does not itself state an iteration or convergence theorem. Strict contraction is not ensured by the stated nonnegativity hypotheses: α=0 or h=0 is allowed and gives q=1. Neither α>0 nor β>0 nor h>0 nor an explicit α≤β or αh≤1 premise is present. The step condition is the product inequality βh≤1, which must not be replaced by division by β when β=0. The sqrt convention must be preserved; a nonnegative radicand is not an explicit hypothesis. The result is about norm distance, not squared distance, objective error, or a stronger unstated contraction factor. Only the supplied anonymous statement and approved definition context were read.

entries.reconstructed_theorem: Let E be any complete real inner product space, with its compatible norm and additive group structure; no finite-dimensional hypothesis is imposed. Let f:E→ℝ and α,β,h∈ℝ be arbitrary. Assume (1) f is continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E; (2) for every x,y∈E and every t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y)−(α/2)t(1−t)‖y−x‖²; (3) α≥0; (4) β≥0; (5) h≥0; (6) βh≤1; and (7) for every x,y∈E, f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖², where ∇f(x) is the Riesz vector representing the derivative of f at x. All these hypotheses hold globally and for the same fixed f,α,β,h. Define T(x)=x−h∇f(x), and q=Real.sqrt(1−αh), the nonnegative real square root with value zero on negative inputs. For every xstar∈E satisfying f(xstar)≤f(y) for every y∈E, for every initial point x₀∈E, and for every natural number N≥0, let x_N=T^[N](x₀), using the same constant h at every step and taking T^[0] to be the identity. Then both inequalities hold: ‖x_N−xstar‖≤q^N‖x₀−xstar‖ and q^N‖x₀−xstar‖≤exp(−αhN/2)‖x₀−xstar‖. N in the exponential is interpreted as a real number. Equivalently these form the displayed chain ‖x_N−xstar‖≤[Real.sqrt(1−αh)]^N‖x₀−xstar‖≤exp(−αhN/2)‖x₀−xstar‖. The conclusion is uniform in the chosen global minimizer, initial point, and iteration number. Its geometric factor and exponential rate depend on α and h; the multiplicative initial-distance factor depends on x₀ and xstar; β occurs only in the hypotheses and admissibility of h. No dimension-dependent or other hidden constant is present.
entries.notes: A global minimizer is supplied conditionally, not proved to exist: the quantifier over xstar precedes an implication from global minimality. The displayed conclusion is a pair of finite-iteration norm inequalities, including N=0. If a minimizer is given and αh>0, the exponential bound yields convergence to that minimizer, but strict positivity is not assumed, so convergence is not guaranteed by this estimate in all admitted cases. In particular α=0 and h=0 are permitted. The statement does not assert minimizer existence or uniqueness, objective-value convergence, variable-step convergence, or a sharper rate. No explicit α≤β or αh≤1 premise is present; preserve the supplied real-square-root convention. βh≤1 must not be rewritten as h≤1/β without handling β=0. Only the supplied anonymous statement and approved definition context were read.
